title: Godot modifies custom resource when it's open inside Inspector on save
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1], v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e]. ### System information Godot v4.6.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8183) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600H with Radeon Graphics (12 threads) - 15.34 GiB memory ### Issue description If you have a custom resource with an inner custom subresource that is defined by an inner class AND the resource (saved in filesystem) is open inside the Inspector and the subresource is expanded and you hit save, Godot will remove all exported fields of your subresource. Resource is defined like this ```gdscript extends Resource class_name MyResource class MySubresource extends Resource: @export var str_data: String @export var pos_data: Vector3 @export var my_sub: MySubresource ``` And you save it like this through a tool script (or a plugin, doesn't matter) ```gdscript ResourceSaver.save(my_res, "res://my_res.tres", ResourceSaver.FLAG_NONE) ``` It will save it like it should Then you open that resource and expand the subresource view Then you hit save (Ctrl + S). Godot will remove all the data of that subresource although it wasn't edited in any way through the editor The editor should not modify custom resources if they weren't changed inside the editor. ### Steps to reproduce Explained above. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [saving_custom_inner_class_resource_2026-03-07_15-47-07.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25814223/saving_custom_inner_class_resource_2026-03-07_15-47-07.zip) Open main.tscn and press "save" tool button on the main node to create the resource. Then open it, expand the subresource and save the scene to erase all data from the subresource.
